messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 route-fanout · 504 spikes + 95th latency > 2.5s in prod · paging oncall now

maya: got the page, I'm looking at the routing cluster first.

sam: oncall — adding context: we rolled traffic split 10% -> new router canary ~30m ago. Might be a bad config.

oliver: checking logs, I see a surge of upstream 504s from the edge -> internal router timeout. attaching filtered logs:
```
2026-01-14T20:07:12Z route-fanout xreq=abcd status=504 upstream=tls-10.23.4.5 latency=1200ms
2026-01-14T20:07:15Z route-fanout xreq=efgh status=504 upstream=tls-10.23.4.6 latency=1900ms
```

maya: thanks. I'm running the quick sanity checks: health endpoints, pod restarts, and netstats. so far pods healthy, no OOMs.

sam: can we flip the canary back to 0%? if the canary is the problem that should stop it.

oliver: preparing command to rollback rollout:
```bash
# k8s rollout undo for router-canary
kubectl -n infra set image deploy/router router=router:stable --record
```

oliver: rolled the canary back to stable at 20:10 UTC. watching metrics now.

jia: support here — we've seen 3 customer tickets from large accounts timing out in the last 15m (acct: Clearwave, Nimbus). non-critical but noticeable error rate spike. I'm drafting a status note for cs.

maya: metrics look better — 95th latency down from 2.6s -> 0.9s over last 6m. error rate nearly back to baseline. good sign.

sre-rotation: can we confirm no data loss and no retry storms? check downstream queues and rate limiter metrics pls.

oliver: downstream queues healthy. no retry fanout from clients observed. rate limiter queued ~stable.

sam: action for immediate mitigation documented: rollback canary (done), ramp down canary flag in router config, watch for recurrence for 1h.

maya: assigning post-incident steps: I'm going to own the postmortem write-up. will create a Jira and capture timeline + hypothesis + next steps. ETA for draft: Tue EOD (3 business days).

jia: I'll handle customer comms follow-up. I'll post the templated note to #support-updates and ping affected accounts.

oliver: I'll add the logs and the rollback command to the incident thread + PR that reverted the image so folks can trace.

sre-rotation: suggested prevention items: add a pre-flight test for canary that simulates fanout load (small synthetic test), and add alert rule to capture canary-only error divergence.

maya: initial action items (captured):
- INF-PLAT-3821: Postmortem doc created by maya (owner: maya) — due: Tue EOD
- INF-PLAT-3822: Add canary preflight synthetic load test (owner: oliver) — due: 2w
- INF-PLAT-3823: Canary divergence alert (owner: sam) — due: 1w
- INF-PLAT-3824: Customer comm follow-up (owner: jia) — due: today

oliver: creating the Jira issues now, will paste links.

oliver: put the Jira links in: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-PLAT-3821 (postmortem), INF-PLAT-3822, INF-PLAT-3823, INF-PLAT-3824

jia: customer comm posted to #support-updates and pinged CS owners. tag: @support.

sam: small retrospective idea — run a 45min brownbag about canary best practices and preflight harness templates. propose next Thu 10:30 PT.

maya: I can present the timeline + lessons learned. want this to be practical (what to test, where to put preflight, and quick rollback playbook).

oliver: I'll demo the small load harness and infra checks.

sre-rotation: count me in for driving the alert rules change. also recommend we include product & support for the brownbag so folks understand customer impact.

maya: poll: who can present next Thu 10:30 PT?

maya: volunteers: maya (present timeline), oliver (demo), jia (customer impact segment). sam/sre-rotation will host Q&A.

sam: LGTM. I'll book the room/calendar and post invite to #eng-all + #support.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged as RECOVERED — page cleared at 20:17 UTC. Postmortem scheduled: INF-PLAT-3821 assigned to maya.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll start the draft and drop the link here when ready. please add any notes or logs you think are relevant. :heart:
